text:
lina (Design): Uploaded a quick Figma link for a side-by-side canary diff view + compact timeline scrub. Trying to address: scan speed for engineers, clear affordance for promoting variants, and SR order for snapshots. https://figma.redwood/abc123 :eyes:

sam (Product): Nice! first pass: canary column feels dense. Can we reduce duplication between snapshot header and timeline row?

greg (Accessibility): Quick checks: contrast of the promo button label is 3.8:1 — fails AA for normal text. Also screen reader order matters: if snapshots are visually side-by-side, SR should announce them sequentially with headings and percentages.

tara (Frontend): Noted on contrast. Also the diff generation on hover could be heavy if we render DOM diffs for every variant. Prefer a lazy-render on focus/keyboard navig.

mike (Eng): Agreed with tara. Also need to consider tokenized payload size for diffs — we can compute a compact summary server-side and send a small delta, then render expanded diffs client-side.

lina (Design): Thoughts on a compact summary row that always shows: name | baseline % | candidate % | quality delta icon. Click to expand the full snapshot diff. Keeps the timeline compact.

sam (Product): Love that. Suggest microcopy change for the promote action: current “Promote to Stable” might read as destructive. Maybe “Promote traffic” with a confirmation step and undo toast.

greg (Accessibility): For announcements, use role="region" and aria-live="polite" for the toast. For the expand/collapse, ensure button has aria-expanded and the expanded panel has aria-labelledby. Also keyboard shortcut hint: add a visible focus ring and docs for 1-2 keyboard commands.

tara (Frontend): Will implement aria-expanded and lazy-render on expand. For keyboard, thinking: Enter toggles, Shift+Arrow to move between snapshots? Might be heavy. Maybe simpler: Tab + Enter to open, Left/Right to move timeline scrubber.

mike (Eng): Left/Right scrubber is fine if we limit event frequency (throttle to 60fps or 100ms). Backend: I can add an endpoint that returns diff-summary objects: {id, baseline_pct, candidate_pct, score_delta, small_html_snippet}.

lina (Design): UX quibble: the timeline scrubber currently overlays the version badges and obscures the hover affordances. Could either nudge the scrubber below the badges or make badges sticky and clickable above the scrubber. Which is simpler?

tara (Frontend): Making badges sticky is straightforward with position: sticky; z-index. But mobile collapse needs special handling — sticky may consume too much viewport.

sam (Product): Prioritize desktop first for next sprint, mobile follow-up. Also we should add an explicit “Compare” mode toggle (side-by-side vs inline diffs). That reduces cognitive load for new users.

greg (Accessibility): In Compare mode, ensure each panel has an accessible label like "Baseline (v3.1)" and "Canary (v3.2)". Screen readers should be able to skip between panels with a single key. Consider adding "Skip to next snapshot" links.

mike (Eng): Implementation question: do we want the compare mode state encoded in the URL so SRE/QA can share specific comparisons? If yes, we'll need to serialize minimal state (variant ids + snapshot id).

lina (Design): Yes please encode in URL — helpful for support. Keep it minimal.

sam (Product): Action items: lina to update Figma with compact summary row + sticky badges option; tara to prototype aria-expanded + lazy-render; mike to spec diff-summary endpoint and URL state; greg to provide checklist for SR order and contrast targets. I'll mark this high priority for the rollout timeline polish.

deploy-bot: Created task RED-UI-4123: "Canary compare: compact summary + a11y fixes" assigned to @lina, @tara, @mike, @greg. Due in 2 weeks.

lina (Design): Thanks — I'll post updated frames by EOD Friday. Quick note: for microcopy alternatives to "Promote traffic" I'm testing "Increase traffic to this variant" vs "Move X% to variant" — any preference?

sam (Product): Prefer concise: "Increase traffic" or just "Promote" with tooltip. Keep it short on buttons.

greg (Accessibility): Button text should still be explicit for screen readers, tooltip helps visuals but SR needs the full intent e.g., "Promote variant: increase traffic to this version".

tara (Frontend): Copy acknowledged. I'll wire the tooltip and accessible label.

mike (Eng): I'll scope the API change and drop a quick PR draft early next week.

lina (Design): Great, thanks everyone. If no blockers I'll iterate and tag ya for a final pass. :thumbsup:
